title: 16th sitting of the 20th Majlis
summary: The sitting opened with attendance, the agenda, acceptance of earlier minutes and the first reading of a bill amending the legal profession law. Most of the part was question time, where members pressed the Minister of Sports, Fitness and Recreation on stalled or delayed football grounds, courts and youth centres across many islands. The minister mostly cited budget limits, contractor and guarantee delays and promised updates. After a recess, members voted 61-0 to debate an urgent matter on rising electricity bills, and that debate was still under way when this part ends. This part covers the second half of the debate on an urgent matter about high electricity bills, submitted by the member for North Galolhu, who was not on the floor to speak. Members from the governing side and the opposition traded views on the causes of high bills and on renewable energy and cable repairs as fixes, and the one-hour debate window then ran out. The House then debated a government bill to amend the Criminal Procedure Act (Law 2016/12), with members discussing police powers over online crime, bail and court delays. The sponsor replied, and the sitting ended early because of a power cut, with the next sitting set for Monday 22 July 2024 at 9:00.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Asked why Kudarikilu football ground sub-base work was budgeted but not tendered, and for a completion date for his island's pitch.
Asked when football grounds in Kamadhoo, Kihaadhoo and Dhonfanu would be finished, as turf work had stopped in places.
In the electricity debate, cited local bills rising sharply after digital meters and urged a study and a flat per-unit rate.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Criticised the previous government's sports record and raised a reported unpaid bill at the football association office; the chair cut him off at the time limit.
Said complaints about high bills long predate this government and that earlier governments announced fixes that did not follow.
Said the current government first approved a renewable energy project and that more clean power is the way to cut bills.
On the Criminal Procedure bill, said earlier governments left the justice system weak, courts are short of space, and a new criminal court division is being prepared.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ismail
positions: Asked when Vilimale's damaged courts and single futsal ground would be fixed, and whether the ministry audited about MVR 600 million spent earlier.
In the electricity debate, questioned the motive for the urgent matter, noted opposition absence, and said the government is working on utilities; remarks continue into part 2.
Agreed laws must keep up with technology but said wide police powers need a way to monitor how they are used.
Drew on his own experience of being charged and held, and asked the committee to build in safeguards.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: Asked when Lhandhoo's stadium and turf work, handed to a contractor in 2022, would become usable after years without facilities.
As bill sponsor, replied that the powers are meant to investigate cybercrime and not to bring politically motivated cases.
Explained the change to the detention article and raised concerns about people held until trial ends.

speakers.name: Adam Shafeeq
positions: Asked when stalled football, handball and gym works in Kumundhoo and Nekurendhoo would restart and finish, and when youth could use them.
Said court delays erode trust in the justice system and thanked the government for the bill.
Asked for the bill to go to committee quickly and be passed soon.

speakers.name: Abdul Hannan Aboobakuru
positions: Asked why Fehendhoo's football ground, already budgeted, had not started.
Said residents of Thulhaadhoo, Goidhoo, Fulhadhoo and Fehendhoo complain of high bills and protests are being held.
Asked the government to explain clearly why bills are rising.

speakers.name: Abdulla Rifau
positions: Asked how many sports projects under the previous government went to unqualified parties, how their budgets were set, and why they remain unstarted.
Welcomed the matter but criticised the mover's absence.
Said Malé's power plants were left unmaintained by earlier governments and expects solar support to lower bills.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Asked when the Vaikaradhoo skate park would start and what cost cutting the ministry had done while political appointees increased.
In the electricity debate, said bills rose from April and proposed a Majlis committee to question utility providers on the cause.

speakers.name: Ahmed Zahir
positions: Asked why the Maduvvari youth centre, due for completion in 140 days from July 2023, is unfinished and when it will open.
Fully supported the amendments, citing global cybercrime losses and a hotel data breach affecting tourists.
Asked for the committee to study the bill and bring in outside expertise.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Asked when Narudhoo's football ground works would start, and how many grounds and courts the previous government completed.
Said it was regrettable that the mover was absent and questioned the sincerity of the submission.
Raised questions about smart-meter billing and called for consumers to be told how bills are calculated.

speakers.name: Ahmed Naseer
positions: Asked when Ihavandhoo's sports arena work would start, noting grounds built earlier in nearby islands had deteriorated.
Said the mover's absence from the floor showed the matter was not treated as urgent by him.
Said the government gave discounts and subsidies and blamed weak networks and limited generating capacity, with outside consultants being sought.

speakers.name: Abdul Latheef Mohamed
positions: Asked when a new youth centre building would be built in Dhidhdhoo, and for fixes to misdirected field lights and road-facing seating.
Said the governing majority accepted the matter and that high bills are felt in every region.
Said no past government fixed it and called on the President to deliver a permanent solution.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Asked whether the ministry would continue the Feydhoo sports arena begun under the previous government, which stalled with only parts of walls built.
In the electricity debate, questioned why digital meters were introduced and urged checking who installed which meters before blaming the new government.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Moved an urgent matter calling on the government to investigate sharply higher STELCO and FENAKA bills and explain them to customers.
After the vote, said the Utility Regulatory Authority is responsible for service standards and rates, and urged accountability.

speakers.name: Ahmed Saleem
positions: On electricity bills, said the mover left the floor and that damaged cables were installed in earlier years; new cables are now being laid.
On the Criminal Procedure bill, said court delays and the bail system leave people jailed for years and wanted stronger measures against offenders.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Asked when the futsal ground in Maamendhoo, reportedly not properly started, would be completed.

speakers.name: Mohamed Niushad
positions: Asked why the Keyodhoo outdoor volleyball court was delayed and when Rakeedhoo's futsal ground work would begin.

speakers.name: Mohamed Dawoodh
positions: Asked when the unfinished zigzag ground rostrum, goal fencing, synthetic track, sports complex and volleyball court in Kulhudhuffushi would proceed and be paid.

speakers.name: Ismail Shafeeu
positions: Asked for updates on Kalaidhoo's futsal ground and Isdhoo's indoor volleyball court, and what became of sports equipment donated earlier.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Asked whether Hithadhoo's 2024 budgeted works would start this year and whether the government will dissolve the Sports Corporation.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Asked whether the previous government was responsible for the football association's financial state, and suggested summoning ministers who miss the three-day answer deadline.

speakers.name: Abdul Sattar Mohamed
positions: Asked when Miladhoo football ground fencing, now needing a height variation, would start after approval.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abdul Rahman
positions: Asked when Hinnavaru's long derelict football ground would be repaired or rebuilt, and when stalled rostrum and seating work would resume.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Asked whether bid documents set a deadline for performance guarantees after award and what happens if one is not submitted.

speakers.name: Mohamed Sinan
positions: Asked the minister to inspect and update on North Hithadhoo's football ground, reported in poor condition for about ten years.

speakers.name: Abdulla Shareef
positions: Asked about Vashafaru ground turf, Fiyaladhoo's handball court, Kelaa's planned indoor complex and missing youth centre staff.

speakers.name: Abdulla Rasheed
positions: Asked about Dhangethi's football ground budgeted in 2022, Omadhoo's volleyball court, the unused Dhigurah youth centre and Mandhoo's lack of sports facilities.

speakers.name: Ahmed Didi
positions: Asked when floodlights at Maradhoo football ground would be fitted, as youth complain they cannot play at night.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shamin Habeeb
positions: Asked about repairing wave-damaged Kurendhoo ground, floodlights promised before the election, and stalled Olhuvelifushi ground wall work.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Said electricity bill problems date back to about 2014-15 tariff changes and expressed confidence the current government will address them.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Said the government promised electricity at a flat rate, and noted STELCO is surveying Hulhumale' North apartment blocks with high air-conditioning use.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Called electricity a basic right, said complaints predate this government, and described FENAKA's finances and spending as problems it inherited.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Muhammad
positions: Disputed that bills triple each month and urged scrutiny of fuel import contracts, citing a reported MVR 271 million loss.

speakers.name: Mohamed Afoo Hamid
positions: Said tariffs were set about 12 years ago and cited a pledge to lower the unit price, blaming earlier handling of the utilities.

speakers.name: Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim
positions: Said high electricity bills have been raised for years and that a Ramadan subsidy lowered bills before later bills rose again.
Said causes of the rises should be studied and expressed confidence that more renewable energy would bring bills down.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Thanked members who voted to accept the matter and said high bills worry households of every party.
Said people need hope, citing long solar waiting lists and unclear rules, and asked for rules to change.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shahid
positions: Said the issue affects all islands and that service providers should give residents better answers to complaints.
Said electricity is a basic service and the matter should not be politicised.

speakers.name: Ahmed Aifan
positions: Said the governing majority took up the matter responsibly and criticised the opposition for leaving the floor.
Said he had met Stelco's managing director and that the lasting fix is renewable energy.

speakers.name: Ahmed Azaan Marzooq
positions: Said the amendments give police useful powers against online crime but include wide powers such as intercepting data and seizing devices.
Asked for safeguards: notifying monitored people, deleting unrelated data, and a way to challenge surveillance in court.

decisions: Minutes of sittings 9 to 13 of 2024 accepted because no amendments were submitted.
First reading held for the bill amending the legal profession law, sponsored by Hussain Shareef.
Urgent matter on electricity bills accepted for debate in the chamber by 61 votes to 0.
The one-hour debate period on the urgent matter on electricity bills ended and the House moved on to unfinished business.
Debate on the Criminal Procedure Act amendment bill (8.1) was held and the sponsor replied; no vote is recorded in this part.
The Deputy Speaker took the chair partway through the urgent-matter debate.
The chair ended the sitting early because a power cut left only backup power, and set the next sitting for Monday 22 July 2024 at 9:00.
